Quiz 3

Amanda Mae Woodward

2025-10-30

  1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
library(readr)
spotDat <- read_csv("spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
## Rows: 2000 Columns: 6
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (3): artist, song, genre
## dbl (3): popularity, danceability, tempo
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
View(spotDat)
  1. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
library(ggplot2)
## Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.5.2
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist))+geom_bar()+theme((axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)))

  1. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()

  1. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3.
library(RColorBrewer)
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme((axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)))+scale_fill_brewer(palette= "Greens")
## Warning in RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n, pal): n too large, allowed maximum for palette Greens is 9
## Returning the palette you asked for with that many colors

  1. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph.
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme(legend.position = "bottom")

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

  1. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
library(dplyr)
## Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 4.5.2
## 
## Attaching package: 'dplyr'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     filter, lag
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
library(tidyr)
## Warning: package 'tidyr' was built under R version 4.5.2
spotWide<- spotDat |> pivot_wider(id_cols=c("artist","tempo","song", "popularity", "danceability"), names_from="genre", values_from="genre", values_fn=list)
  1. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format.
spotLong<- spotWide |> pivot_longer(cols=c(colnames(spotWide)[6:64]), names_to="genres", values_to="song genre")

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre

spotGraph<- ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+ geom_bar()+theme((axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)))
spotGraph+facet_wrap(~genre)

  1. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability.
ggplot(spotDat, aes(tempo, danceability))+geom_point(shape=4)+theme_bw()

  1. Add popularity as a third variable.
library(viridis)
## Loading required package: viridisLite
ggplot(spotDat, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity))+geom_point(shape=4)+theme_dark()

  1. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
library(viridis)
ggplot(spotDat, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity))+geom_point(shape=4)+scale_color_viridis(discrete=FALSE, option="plasma")
